[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Digital Realty is a publicly traded data center real estate investment trust. This session sourced two acquisitions that explain building names appearing across this operators rows in this registry. Per Data Center Dynamics trade press, Digital Realty completed a 7.8 billion dollar all-stock merger with DuPont Fabros Technology on September 15, 2017, adding 12 facilities concentrated in Ashburn, Virginia, which is why several Ashburn buildings in this registry still carry DuPont Fabros own ACC, meaning Ashburn Corporate Campus, naming convention. Separately, per Data Center Knowledge trade press, Digital Realty acquired the East Coast data center operations of AboveNet Inc. on October 2, 2006, for 40 million dollars, including a leased facility at 8100 Boone Boulevard, Vienna, Virginia, which is this registrys 8100 Boone Boulevard row. This specific row, Digital Realty IAD41, Building P, matches a datacenterHawk listing whose own building code and letter exactly match this rows name, giving 44751 Round Table Plaza, Ashburn, VA.

reading.body:
Digital Realty IAD41 is a single building in Ashburn, Virginia, part of the operator's Northern Virginia campus that spans at least six named buildings across Loudoun and surrounding counties. The operator publishes approximately 600 MW of IT load across this entire Northern Virginia footprint as of 2023, but does not publish a building-specific figure for IAD41. Without a confirmed capacity number for this building alone, its scale within the campus cannot be determined from published sources.

Virginia hosts 326 mapped data center facilities, of which 23 have published megawatt figures totaling 1375.4 MW. Digital Realty's entire Northern Virginia campus ranks 24th by published capacity in the state, meaning it represents a significant but not leading share of Virginia's declared data center power. The campus sits in Data Center Alley, the densest colocation region in the United States by count of major facilities.

IAD41's role in AI scaling depends on whether it hosts accelerator-dense workloads and what power density its electrical infrastructure can support. No certifications, power distribution specifications, cooling standards, or tenant information are published for this building. The address is confirmed through third-party colocation marketplace listings, but without building-level capacity data or network documentation, this site cannot assess whether IAD41 represents available AI-ready infrastructure or existing committed load.
